name: American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California v. Superior Court
court: California Court of Appeal, First District
summary: The ACLU sought ALPR data (license plate reader records) collected by law enforcement agencies. The agencies refused disclosure citing the law enforcement investigative records exemption under § 6254(f) (now § 7923.650). The court examined whether bulk ALPR records — which lack individualized investigative purpose for most plates captured — qualify for the law enforcement exemption.
holding: ALPR records collected without individualized suspicion may not automatically qualify for the § 6254(f) law enforcement investigative records exemption. The law enforcement exemption is not a blanket shield for all records possessed by law enforcement agencies; agencies must demonstrate that the specific records relate to a specific investigation and that disclosure would endanger witnesses or reveal confidential investigative techniques. Mass-collected surveillance data requires particularized showing.

legal_definitions.definition: Under § 6254(f) / § 7923.650, records of investigations conducted by any state or local police agency are exempt from CPRA if disclosure would endanger the safety of a person involved in an investigation, disclose the identity of a confidential informant, or constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.
legal_definitions.context: The exemption requires particularized showing, not automatic application to all records held by law enforcement.

relevance_to_audit: Directly applicable to CPRA requests for ALPR data in Tulare County and other ODIA audit jurisdictions. Law enforcement agencies that cite § 6254(f) / § 7923.650 to withhold bulk ALPR records must make a particularized showing that disclosure would harm investigations — a blanket § 6254(f) claim for all ALPR data is presumptively insufficient under this case.

key_quotes.text: The law enforcement exemption under § 6254(f) requires agencies to show that the specific records at issue relate to a pending or prospective law enforcement investigation, and that disclosure would compromise witness safety, informant identities, or investigative techniques.
key_quotes.context: Rejecting a blanket § 6254(f) claim over bulk surveillance records without investigation nexus.

procedural_posture: Petition for writ of mandate to compel disclosure; granted in part
subsequent_treatment: Cited for the proposition that § 6254(f) requires particularized showing; subsequent Civil Code § 1798.90.51-55 (SB 34) enacted to address ALPR data governance
